questions.answer: PPROT is a direct copy of AxPROT with no translation. The bridge does no local privilege check. System policy is TBD, but it is enforced by the APB Completers and does not alter PPROT in the bridge.

A request is rejected if it has an unsupported AxSIZE (not 0/1/2), an unsupported or reserved burst or length, an AxCACHE other than 0000/0001, or a 4-KiB crossing. The response is SLVERR, never DECERR. No APB access is issued. A read returns ARLEN+1 R beats. A write drains its W beats and returns one B.

At most one read or write transaction is active at a time. Reads and writes do not interleave. If AR and AW are both pending, they are serialized by round-robin grant. AR wins the first tie after reset, and the preference flips after each completed transaction. The owner keeps the bridge until its final R or B handshake.
Yes. The tie preference flips after each completed transaction. The spec makes no exception for rejected transactions or for transactions that had no tie.

Yes. An AxCACHE other than 0000/0001 makes the request unsupported. A rejected write drains AWLEN+1 W beats with no APB and returns one SLVERR B. A rejected read returns ARLEN+1 SLVERR R beats with RLAST on the final beat only, and issues no APB access.
Yes. Write PSLVERR accumulates. Later beats still execute on APB. The final BRESP is SLVERR after all declared W beats.

The bridge is an AXI4 Subordinate on the AXI side (the AXI Manager is the peer). It is an APB4 Manager/Requester on the APB side (APB Completers are the peers). Each rule follows from which interface its signals belong to.

The bridge has no timeout. It holds the APB access while PREADY=0 and waits indefinitely. It is verified with wait-state assertions (TEST-003) that APB control/payload stays stable during the wait. Formal liveness assumes the APB eventually becomes ready. The two rules are the same behavior seen from two sides.
PARA_AXI_ID_W is legal from 1 to 16, with default 4, and an invalid value is an elaboration error. It sets both read and write ID widths. Verification must sweep widths 1, 4 and 16, not only 4.

The AxLOCK, USER, QOS and REGION ports are omitted, so no such signals exist to respond to. Exclusive access is not implemented, and integration must not send exclusive traffic. No exclusive response is defined because that traffic is outside the profile.

The spec says APB transfers are sequential and that pipelined transactions are excluded, so there is no pipelining. It does not say whether an idle or gap cycle is required or allowed between consecutive APB transfers. The designer must specify this.

The spec states round-robin only for the case when both AR and AW are pending. It does not explicitly state the grant behavior when only one is pending. Nor does it state how the pointer is updated at grant time as opposed to completion. The designer must define these.

Legal write count is AWLEN+1. An unsupported length or burst is rejected: no APB, drain the W beats, one SLVERR B. A W count that mismatches AWLEN, such as a WLAST mismatch, is a malformed AXI Manager violation. It is outside the guaranteed profile, with no RTL recovery or defined response.

Yes, it applies to writes too. A 4-KiB crossing is rejected without APB for both reads and writes. A rejected write drains the declared W beats, makes no APB access, and returns one SLVERR B after the final W.

AXI4 prohibits a crossing burst, so it is not legal AXI stimulus. The bridge defensively rejects it before any APB traffic, so its behavior is defined: SLVERR with no APB. It is a tested boundary case (WF-013), not part of the generic undefined malformed-AXI profile.

Yes. Reset in any state returns to IDLE and clears local state. AXI VALIDs and READYs are 0 in reset. APB PSEL and PENABLE are 0, and PADDR, PWDATA and the other APB outputs are 0 (idle). An interrupted transfer is canceled. Completion or rollback of an in-flight AXI response or APB access is not guaranteed.

Reset is synchronous. It is sampled on the rising clock edge, with synchronous assertion. Outputs take their reset values (VALID=0, PSEL/PENABLE=0) after the clock edge that samples reset active, not combinationally on reset assertion.

The spec lists the three labels (Parameter Description, Parameter values, Parameter unit) and says they immediately precede the declaration. It does not say whether the order is mandatory, or whether other comments or blank lines may sit between them and the declaration.
The spec only says an invalid PARA_AXI_ID_W is an elaboration error. It does not specify the mechanism ($error, generate assertion, etc.) or the expected tool behavior. The designer must decide.

Address, data and APB widths are fixed at 32 bits. Every other port width is fixed in the port list, for example WSTRB and PSTRB at 4 bits, LEN at 8 bits and PROT at 3 bits. Only the ID width is parameterized.

Yes. Reject means no APB access. A read returns ARLEN+1 R beats with SLVERR. A write drains the W beats and returns one SLVERR B. This applies to 4-KiB crossing, a reserved or unsupported AxBURST, and an AxCACHE other than 0000/0001.

The Manager is the AXI Manager, the source of AXI address, size and WSTRB. It must assert only legal lanes and must select the requested bytes from the bus lanes using the AXI address and size. The bridge passes WSTRB to PSTRB unchanged and applies no lane rotation.

Unsupported is defined as: AxSIZE not 0/1/2, a reserved AxBURST, or a length outside FIXED 1–16, INCR 1–256 or WRAP 2/4/8/16. It also covers AxCACHE other than 0000/0001 and 4-KiB crossing. Each is handled by the REJECT_READ or REJECT_WRITE path.
Yes. Reset discards local state, and AR is chosen on the first tie after reset. The preference then flips after each completed transaction.
Yes. In REJECT_WRITE the bridge drains the declared W count with no APB, and B (SLVERR) comes only after the final W. W may arrive before AW, but WREADY stays low until AW is accepted.

Reset cancels in-flight local state: outstanding R/B work is discarded and APB is deselected. Outputs go to the reset values (VALID=0, PSEL/PENABLE=0). Completion or rollback of an interrupted transfer is not guaranteed. The SoC coordinates reset with the AXI Manager and APB fabric.

The bridge does no address decode. The external default error Completer in the APB fabric drives PREADY=1/PSLVERR=1. The bridge then handles it as an ordinary PSLVERR, giving SLVERR on a read beat or accumulated into BRESP on a write. A missing default responder is an integration violation.

Reset is sampled synchronously, so PSEL/PENABLE go to 0 after the active reset edge, not asynchronously. The in-flight transfer is canceled and its completion is not guaranteed. The SoC must coordinate the reset between the AXI Manager and the APB fabric.

Stability applies to the APB control and payload signals while PREADY=0: PADDR, PWRITE, PPROT, PWDATA, PSTRB, PSEL and PENABLE. It also applies to AXI VALID/payload through the handshake. The R payload (RID, RDATA, RRESP, RLAST) and B payload (BID, BRESP) stay stable while VALID=1 and READY=0. The stall conditions are APB PREADY=0, RREADY=0 and BREADY=0.

Legal sizes are AxSIZE 0/1/2 (1/2/4 bytes). Burst lengths are FIXED 1–16, INCR 1–256 and WRAP 2/4/8/16. The AXI address is byte-addressed, and APB PADDR is aligned down to the 4-byte word (bits [1:0] cleared). A burst must not cross a 4-KiB boundary. FIXED holds the address, and INCR and WRAP follow the AXI address rules.

APB PSLVERR maps to AXI SLVERR, never OKAY and not DECERR. A read marks the R beat of that transfer SLVERR. A write accumulates the error into the final BRESP=SLVERR. The mapping is the same value (SLVERR) for both, but the write error is aggregated across beats.

The behavior is defined: reset cancels local state with no replay or rollback. In-flight AXI and APB transfers are canceled, and completion is not guaranteed. The assumption's status is still 'Integration confirmation needed', so it is not yet confirmed.

Malformed writes (WLAST mismatch, illegal WSTRB lanes) are outside the guaranteed profile. The Manager must comply with AXI4, and no RTL recovery or expected behavior is defined. Verification therefore has nothing to check for such traffic and should keep stimulus AXI-legal.

The decoder and default error Completer are external, in the SoC/APB fabric, and the SoC integrator owns them (address map, default PREADY=1/PSLVERR=1). They are outside the RTL. The testbench must still model the unmapped-address default response, since TEST-004 injects APB errors and unmapped addresses and REQ-ERR-004 is verified by integration test.
